summary: This division was covered by the dedicated country dossier, which found no Uttarākhand-specific trans law, enforcement series or incident pattern and records it among the states/UTs that have not constituted the mandated transgender welfare board; the national legal position (no state criminalisation, uniform 2019 Act as amended in 2026) applies without material deviation (±0.02), so it is assessed at the national score.

sources.summary: Human Rights Watch statement (26 March 2026) on India's 2026 Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Bill passed by parliament: removes self-identification, restricts recognition to hijra/kinner and intersex categories, mandates medical certification, and creates offences carrying up to life imprisonment for "coercing or alluring" someone to be transgender. National framework applying uniformly in Uttarākhand; no state-specific reporting.

BBC report (26 March 2026): the amendment removing self-identification passed both houses amid protests, adds mandatory medical-board certification for gender-affirming surgery, drew a withdrawal request from a Supreme Court-appointed advisory panel, and awaits presidential assent. Applies nationally including Uttarākhand; the piece has no regional angle.

Times of India (Kolkata, 18 August 2024): alleged "gender check" groping of a transwoman by an RPF constable at a Kolkata metro station, denied by the RPF with a counter-FIR. A West Bengal incident kept here as a national datapoint on security-forces screening of gender-nonconforming people, not an Uttarākhand finding.
